title: Beyond Suspicious Steps: Delegation Trust in Long-Horizon Agents
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Detection signal quality varies widely across scoring methods and backbone models, with no single signal uniformly reliable.
layout: single 3x9 heatmap, models as rows, signals as columns, diverging colorbar
description: A single heatmap with three rows for backbone LLMs (Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, GPT-4o-mini) and nine columns for deviation or monitoring signals. These include LLM-based Evaluator, State Transition Operator, Predictive Entropy, Role Energy, Causal Grounding, Temporal Context Dynamics, Logical Consistency Constraint, Role-Energy Delta and Causal Trace Consistency. Each cell shows a bold AUC percentage. Cells are colored on a diverging scale: blue for high AUC (about 70 or more) and red for low AUC (about 46 to 52). A colorbar labeled AUC (%) sits on the right. Column labels are rotated diagonally. The eye goes first to the saturated red and blue cells, such as Predictive Entropy for GPT-4o-mini at 46.64 and Causal Grounding for Llama at 73.49.
caption: Snapshot-level AUC heatmap on Living-off-the-Land trajectories.
abstract: Long-horizon agents increasingly operate across many steps, tools, and observa- tions. In this setting, the relevant oversight question is not only whether each action is locally valid, but whether the evolving trajectory still corresponds to the task the user authorized. Drift can accumulate quietly. An agent may call the right tool with plausible arguments at every step, while its prefix moves toward a broader role, an adjacent objective, or evidence unsupported by the task or observed environment. Existing monitors mostly check local compliance, deliver final-trace verdicts, or score generic risk; they typically do not directly estimate this prefix-level relation. We formulate task-delegation consistency, the relation between an authorized task and its execution prefix, and instantiate it as RGE, an online monitor of deviations along Role, Goal, and Evidence. RGE uses LLMs only to derive structured task and step representations; deviation-state updates, projections, and alarm decisions are deterministic, yielding a replayable and auditable deviation trajectory given recorded parser outputs. We construct a cross-domain trajectory corpus from OS- World, FinanceBench, and EICU-AC, covering benign executions, prefix-paired drift, and pseudo-consistency failures. Under the evaluated default protocols, RGE achieves higher benchmark-averaged Drift F1 than the adapted rule-, judge-, and shield-style baselines with GPT-4o and Qwen3.5-9B. With these two estimators, it exceeds 93% Drift F1 on every benchmark while keeping benign coverage at or above 95.8%. Pseudo-consistency, however, remains harder to detect, with performance varying across domains.
